elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph covers only "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $1,000,000 and cyber liability and privacy insurance of not less than $2,000,000"; no commercial general liability coverage or per-occurrence limit appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No CGL aggregate limit is stated; the insertion contains no general liability line at all.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O is set at "not less than $1,000,000", below the preferred USD 2,000,000 threshold.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The Servicer handles Obligor account and payment information, so the condition applies, but cyber/privacy coverage is only "not less than $2,000,000", short of USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: The insertion is silent on workers' compensation; no statutory coverage covenant is added.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: No certificate-delivery mechanic is inserted; the paragraph ends after the cyber limit.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The Servicer will maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $1,000,000" — an affirmative covenant on Cellco as Servicer at the fallback amount, in the Agreement's dollar denomination.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "and cyber liability and privacy insurance of not less than $2,000,000" — expressly covers both cyber and privacy at the fallback limit.

reasons: The finding is correctly scored as missing: the document's only insurance references are Obligor insurance premiums billed to wireless accounts and FDIC deposit insurance in the "Qualified Institution" definition, neither of which is a Servicer coverage covenant.

Both fallback elements are met in operative language by a single inserted sentence, so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level; the preferred level fails on four separate limits plus workers' compensation and certificates.

Minimality holds: the insertion adds no survival tail, no "at its own expense" language, no certificate-delivery or notice-of-cancellation procedure, and no additional insured or waiver-of-subrogation extras beyond the two selected fallback elements. Section 10.13 and the surrounding Regulation AB text are reproduced verbatim with no deletions or paraphrase.
Intent is preserved: the new covenant is free-standing, introduces no defined term, cross-reference, or timing mechanic, and does not contradict any retained allocation in Article X.

Drafting notes (not failures): the rationale says the insert is "Section 10.14" but the rendered text carries only an unnumbered "Insurance." heading — number it 10.14 so it slots cleanly after 10.13. Also consider writing "USD 1,000,000"/"USD 2,000,000" rather than bare "$" for consistency with the playbook, and consider binding "Cellco, in each of its capacities as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian" rather than "the Servicer" alone, since the Custodian capacity is where Obligor records are held.

If negotiating room exists, note in the comment that the preferred package (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) remains our position and that this is the fallback.
